$comment: API requests a hard load of each dashboard page may send (research/81). A page not listed gets defaultMax. Lower a number when a page gets cheaper; raising one needs a reviewer to agree the new request cannot come from the bootstrap, the cache or an event.
$comment_security: /account/security reads the account's own sign-in methods (one request, GET /api/v1/me/sign-in-methods): they are per account and change only by the person's own link or unlink, so neither the bootstrap nor the cache holds them.
$comment_counts: /scope reads its strip, tab and approval counts from two one-row lists with include=status_counts (entries, exclusions) next to its table; /compliance reads every framework card's stats from the frameworks list (include=stats); /sensors reads the fleet and its stats in one poll-mode request (changed_since), which its 15 s refresh repeats with only the changed sensors.
$comment_posture: /attack-surface sends the bootstrap, the suggestion count, the summary, the stats, the monitoring settings and the posture score (GET /api/v1/attack-surface/posture, one precomputed row per organization). The score is per organization and changes on the posture refresh schedule, so neither the bootstrap nor the cache holds it; folding it into the summary would couple two cards that refresh on different schedules.
$comment_attention: /assets/attention lists five reasons with a count each. The counts come from the queues' own caller-scoped list endpoints (three asset lists with per_page=1, the suggestion count, the duplicate reviews), so a number never covers assets the reader cannot open; one summary endpoint (research/233 P1) would replace them. 10 matches /assets, which sends a similar set of list requests.
$comment_pageUses: A page that needs one of those endpoints for its own content, not for the shell: the change-password card reads the password policy from /auth/providers.
$comment_sensorSafety: /settings/scanning/sensor-safety loads the opt-in impact, shared-sensor setting, tenant settings, identity policy and the last-changed audit line, plus the support-access banner.
$comment_settingsAi: /settings/ai shows five independent resources on open (AI settings, AI config, sources, AI agents, masking) and two more cards that each read their own tenant-scoped resource: the auto-triage policy and the knowledge sources list. None of them can come from the bootstrap (they are admin-only reads that change on save) and each card reads only its own endpoint, so the page is budgeted at seven.
$comment_supportAccess: The support-access banner (a shell element on every page) takes the active grants from /me/bootstrap and sends no request on a load (it re-reads once a minute afterwards), so a page budget counts only the page's own reads; /settings/members also loads join requests and the ownership transfer.
$comment_scans: /scans lists the scans the platform runs itself (continuous coverage) in a read-only section above the table: GET /api/v1/scans?origin=system&per_page=10&sort=name. It is a different query from the paginated, filtered table (page 1 of 25 mixes both origins), changes with every coverage run (not bootstrap data), is not cached on a hard load and has no event, so the page needs one more request (7 to 8). With the origin filter on System the section is not rendered and the table serves both.
$comment_dynamicRoutes: Pages with an id in their path (research/335, RFC-136). Every such page must be listed: the gate loads it for the first item of `sample` (an API list) or the first link to it on the list page `from`, and skips it when the seed has none. /findings/[id] loads through GET /findings/{id}/view: the bootstrap, the view, the asset's SLA policy and the support-access banner. Pages the e2e seed has no item for carry defaultMax until a seed item or the page's own change measures them. /assets/[id] loads through GET /assets/{id}/view (the asset and its panels' reads, the ports on a name's resolved addresses included); its budget stays 12 until a measured run lowers it.
